title: Identification of Methyl Isocyanate and Other Complex Organic Molecules in a Hot Molecular Core, G31.41+0.31
question: Which complex organic molecules (including new detections of CH3NCO and CH3SH) are present in the hot molecular core G31.41+0.31, what are their column densities, temperatures and abundances, and what do infall and outflow tracers say about its kinematics

evidence.quote: G31.41+0.31 (hereafter G31) is an HMC that is thought to be located at a 7.9 kpc distance from the Earth (cite: chur90).

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum, image continuum and fit its size and flux
recipe.method: uvcontsub with first-order baseline fit to separate continuum and line data; two-dimensional Gaussian fit to the dust continuum
key_parameters: peak 158.4 mJy/beam, integrated flux 242.4 mJy, rms 5 mJy/beam
assumptions: Source treated as unresolved or at best marginally resolved; beam dilution correction applied to brightness temperature

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column density and dust optical depth from the continuum
recipe.method: Optically thin dust continuum equation N_H2 = (S_beam/Omega_beam)/(2 kappa B_nu(T_d) Z mu_H m_H), with brightness-temperature check of optical depth
assumptions: dust-to-gas ratio Z = 0.01, mu_H = 1.41, dust temperature 150 K

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and measure line parameters
recipe.method: Spectra extracted from a 1.1 arcsec diameter circular region at the phase centre; single Gaussian fits for FWHM, V_LSR and integrated intensity; multi-Gaussian fits for blended CH3SH profiles
key_parameters: CH3SH multi-Gaussian: fixed velocity separation and line-intensity ratio, FWHM free
assumptions: Line identification with CDMS and JPL spectroscopic databases

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperatures with rotation diagrams
recipe.method: Linear fit of log(N_u/g_u) versus E_u for CH3OH, CH3OCHO, CH3SH and CH3NCO; two temperature components fitted for methanol
key_parameters: T_rot: CH3OCHO ~162 K, CH3SH 76 K, CH3NCO 48 K, CH3OH cold 33 K and hot 181 K

recipe.goal: Derive molecular column densities and abundances with LTE modeling
recipe.method: CASSIS LTE model spectra compared with observed spectra; only column density varied, with Tex, source size, FWHM and N_H2 fixed; beam-averaged column density; abundances relative to H2
key_parameters: Source size set to the deconvolved continuum size; FWHM from Gaussian fits; Tex assumed ~150 K
assumptions: Beam dilution not taken into account in the beam-averaged column density; abundances relative to N_H2 = 1.53e25 cm-2

recipe.goal: Constrain density and temperature from absorption lines with non-LTE radiative transfer
recipe.method: RADEX grid over n_H = 1e3-1e7 cm-3 and T_kin = 1-100 K for HCN (1-0), H13CO+ (1-0), SiO (2-1) with a 36 K continuum background
assumptions: Collisional rates from LAMDA; spectroscopic constants from JPL/CDMS

recipe.method: Infall velocity from the offset of the H13CO+ red-shifted absorption from the systemic velocity; SiO and HCN blue/red lobes imaged and outflow velocity, dynamical time, mass, momentum and energy derived
key_parameters: Outflow velocity taken as maximum outflow velocity relative to 97 km/s LSR; SiO blue/red lobe velocities 23 and 33 km/s
assumptions: Same abundance 1.0e-8 and excitation temperature 20 K for SiO and HCN; distance 7.9 kpc, with values for 3.7 kpc given in parentheses

recipe.goal: Compare abundances with other hot cores and a chemical model
recipe.method: Compare G31 column densities, abundances and molecular ratios with Sgr B2(N), Orion KL, G10.47+0.03 and the hot-core model peak gas-phase abundances at 100-200 K (fast warm-up)
assumptions: Fast warm-up timescale model judged most suitable for high-mass star-forming regions
